external_entities.name: colleagues
external_entities.description: Colleagues who sign in through the identity broker.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.
external_entities.notes: The source does not state how colleagues authenticate or whether they use a second factor.

external_entities.name: franchise colleagues
external_entities.description: Colleagues from franchise stores who use their own identity provider.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The source does not place franchise colleagues in a specific zone.

external_entities.name: franchise identity provider
external_entities.description: An identity provider operated by the franchise organization that vouches for franchise colleagues.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in
external_entities.notes: The source does not state which colleagues this provider is allowed to vouch for or where the provider runs.

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: The HR system that supplies colleague and group membership changes to the broker.
external_entities.source_excerpt: it comes from the HR system overnight
external_entities.notes: The source does not place the HR system in a specific zone.

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, accepts federated sign-ins, supplies public signing keys, pulls HR changes, and writes sign-ins to an audit log.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: The source does not state whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

processes.name: applications
processes.description: Applications that consume broker-issued tokens and decide what colleagues may do from the groups in the tokens.
processes.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.
processes.notes: The source describes applications generically and does not identify their individual implementations.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: An application that authorizes holders of store-manager tokens to change prices and void transactions across every store.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications.
processes.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: A key store holding the signing key used by the identity broker to sign tokens.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.
data_stores.notes: The source does not state whether the key store is encrypted where it sits.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory containing colleagues and their group memberships.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_stores.notes: Group membership is supplied from the HR system overnight. The source does not state whether the directory is encrypted where it sits.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: A log to which the broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route. The source also does not state whether the log is encrypted where it sits.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: Colleagues sign in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.
data_flows.notes: The authentication mechanism and transport are not stated.

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token to a signed-in colleague.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.notes: The token carries the colleague's staff id and a list of the groups they are in.
data_flows.data_description: A token carrying the colleague's staff id and group membership.

data_flows.name: present token
data_flows.description: A colleague presents the broker-issued token to an application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.
data_flows.notes: The source does not state the protocol or transport protection.
data_flows.data_description: A broker-issued token containing a staff id and group membership.

data_flows.name: use console
data_flows.description: A colleague uses the store admin console with a token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.
data_flows.notes: The console works against every store and does not check which store the colleague belongs to.
data_flows.data_description: A store-manager token and price or transaction administration actions.

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: Applications fetch the public half of the broker's signing key.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.notes: The source does not state the protocol or transport protection.
data_flows.data_description: The public half of the token-signing key.

data_flows.name: store signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker keeps its signing key in the key store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_flows.name: pull changes
data_flows.description: The identity broker pulls colleague and group membership changes from the HR system overnight.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night
data_flows.notes: The source states that the broker initiates the pull but does not state the protocol or transport protection.

data_flows.name: update directory
data_flows.description: The identity broker updates its directory with colleagues and their group memberships.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: vouch for sign-in
data_flows.description: Franchise colleagues use their own identity provider for sign-in.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them

data_flows.name: federated sign-in
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for a franchise colleague and the broker accepts that as a sign-in.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in
data_flows.notes: The source does not state which colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.
data_flows.data_description: A federated sign-in assertion for a franchise colleague.

data_flows.name: write sign-in
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-ins to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: The source does not state what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network on which the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: home devices
trust_boundaries.description: Colleagues' own devices at home from which they sign in.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

trust_boundaries.name: franchise stores
trust_boundaries.description: The franchise-store environment admitted to the system.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

assumptions.assumption: The key store's contents are confidential because it holds the token-signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the key store holds a signing key.

assumptions.assumption: The directory's contents are confidential because it holds colleagues and their group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the directory contains colleagues and the groups they are in.
